claim: Dragging a lightness slider on a ramp with no `lightness` writes an object instead of the two-number tuple

triage.scenario: Take a lightness ramp whose `lightness` is absent, or anything other than an array. `LightnessParams` (layers/RampsLayer.tsx:79) still draws "First L" / "Last L" sliders at 0, because `readParam` answers undefined. Dragging one runs `writeParam(entry, 'lightness.0', v)`. The `top` there is not an array, so the call falls through to `{ ...undefined, '0': v }` and writes `lightness: { "0": v }`. derive requires `Array.isArray(l) && l.length === 2` (packages/theme/src/engine/entries.ts:117), so the ramp stays invalid however the slider moves. The array case only works once the tuple already exists.
triage.cause: object fallback used for an array-shaped parameter

Click-to-inspect counts token declarations inside an unmet @container, @scope or @starting-style rule as applying to the element

triage.scenario: `applies` tests only `CSSMediaRule` and `CSSSupportsRule`; every other grouping rule returns true and its nested rules are visited. A component styled with `@container (min-width: 40rem) { .x { color: var(--wzl-fg-strong) } }` inside a narrow preview pane has that declaration counted, and by source order it can beat the declaration actually in force, so the inspector lists `fg-strong` and jumps to it although the element reads something else. Unmet conditional rules other than media/supports should not contribute (or, where untestable, should not override a declaration known to apply).
triage.cause: conditional-rule check covers only media and supports

claim: Jumping from the inspector to an inherited pins-only token opens the Pins page, which does not list that token

triage.scenario: The draft is a child of weasel (like `fixtures.ts`'s `child`). Inspect a component that reads a token weasel only pins, which the child does not pin itself (one of the `radius-*` pins other than `radius-md`). derive records it as `{ layer: 'pins', pinned: false }` (packages/theme/src/engine/derive.ts:120). `jumpLayerFor` skips the own-pin branch, because the child does not hold the pin, and falls through to `provenance.layer`, which is `'pins'`. `layerNames('pins')` lists only `def.pins` (model.ts:79), so the workbench switches to a Pins page with no row for the token, and nothing is highlighted or scrolled to. The token also appears on no other page. Expected: the jump lands on a page that lists the token, or the Pins page lists inherited pins that apply.
triage.cause: the jump target and the page listing disagree about inherited pure pins

PinRepair converts a numeric pin's text per keystroke, so a decimal cannot be typed and a cleared or signed value turns the pin into a string for good
A draft left for a theme whose file was deleted becomes an undiscardable theme entry that can only fail to reload

triage.scenario: theme `foo` is saved (draft stored with `baseHash: "<sha>"`), then `foo.json` is deleted on disk. On load, `withUnsavedDrafts` re-adds `foo` from its draft with `hash: ''`, and `start` is the stored draft, so `baseHash` is the old sha, not null. The workbench treats it as on-disk: the dead-draft screen offers only "Discard the draft and reload from disk", whose `api.get('foo')` throws; the healthy screen offers no discard at all, and a save with the stale base hash answers a conflict whose "Reload from disk" fails the same way. The theme cannot be dropped from the UI. Should: a theme not in `listed` with `hash === ''` is treated as unsaved (baseHash null / discard offered) whatever its draft says.
triage.cause: draft's baseHash trusted over the list

claim: Click-to-inspect never counts tokens read by ::before / ::after rules, so tokens used only by an element's pseudo-elements go unreported

triage.scenario: a kit control draws part of itself in a pseudo-element, for example `.switch::before { background: var(--wzl-…) }` for a thumb or a checkbox mark. `el.matches('.switch::before')` is false for the element, so `specificityAt` drops the rule and `tokensReadAt` leaves out the token the visible part reads. With Inspect on, clicking the Switch or Checkbox in the preview lists only the host element's tokens, and the jump skips the token the user actually sees. What should happen: match the selector with its pseudo-element stripped and count its declarations for that element.
triage.cause: pseudo-element selectors never match an element

triage.scenario: A semantic rule is `{ by: 'density', comfortable: …, compact: … }`. The drawer labels the toggle `Varies by density` (`axis = rule.by`). Turn it off, and the rule collapses to the current branch. Turn it back on: `setVaries(true)` always writes `{ by: 'mode', …modeValues }`, so the rule now varies by mode rather than density, and a toggle that just read "Varies by density" has silently changed axis. claim: A pinned semantic with no generated value shows `undefined` as its "Rule produced" text

triage.scenario: `produced: text(p.pinned ? p.generated?.value : token.value)`. `text` is `JSON.stringify` for any non-string, and `JSON.stringify(undefined)` returns `undefined`, not a string. So for a pinned token whose provenance has no `generated` (entries.ts:37 treats `pinned && generated === undefined` as a real case), `produced` is `undefined` although `SemanticCell.produced` is typed `string`. SemanticDrawer then draws an empty `<code>` under "Rule produced" where it should show "—", as the Pin column does for a missing value.

claim: A categorical ramp's plain `surface` gate is neither editable nor shown in the gates editor

The editor never shows the surface the ramp is gated against, and nothing can change it. The read-only branch does list it (`values` from `entry.gates`). claim: A reload while the theme draft does not derive drops the whole undo history
Step lists are read without the theme's scope in three places and with it in three others
"Copy as tokens" emits duplicate keys when a pinned anchor shares a name with a generated swatch
A saved undo history containing a malformed step crashes the page at mount on every load

triage.scenario: localStorage holds a history under `weasel.theme-editor.palette-history` (or a theme's `draft-history.<name>`) whose `undoStack` is an array but one entry lacks `forwardOps`, or whose first op has no `args` (a hand edit, a format change, a truncated write). `savedHistoryOf` only checks that `undoStack`/`redoStack` are arrays and `version === 1`, so the save is accepted. `stepsBackTo` runs outside the `try` that guards `restore`, and reads `stack[i]!.forwardOps[0]` and `(first.args as SwapArgs).before` unguarded, so it throws a TypeError inside `useMemo`. The palette lab or theme workbench fails to render, and because nothing clears the key, it fails again on every reload. It should drop the unreadable history, as the strict-restore `catch` already does for a step that cannot be rebuilt.
triage.cause: validation outside the try that guards restore

claim: Inspector ignores inline declarations, so it reports a stylesheet token that has lost the cascade to an inline style

triage.scenario: a kit component in the preview sets a property or a custom property in its `style` attribute (e.g. `style={{ '--thumb-color': 'var(--wzl-accent)' }}` or `background: var(--wzl-x)`). `tokensReadAt` only walks `sheets`' rules, so a token read through the inline declaration is never reported, and a stylesheet declaration the inline one overrides is reported as the winner, listing a token the element does not actually read. The cascade gives the style attribute precedence over all non-`!important` author rules; it should be seeded into `winners[i]` from `el.style` (or `getAttribute('style')`) with a specificity above any selector.
triage.cause: cascade model omits the style attribute

claim: A saved history whose last step is a coalesced burst is dropped instead of stepped back to the state the page opens on

triage.scenario: The theme editor stores a draft only while it derives, so after a reload it opens on the last draft that derived. Its saved history ends on the newer state, and `stepsBackTo` should find how many undos lead back. It reads `forwardOps[0].args.before` of each entry. But `coalesceEntry` (packages/history/src/entryOps.ts:124) sets `top.forwardOps = ops` on every merge. A coalesced entry's `forwardOps[0]` is therefore the *last* tick's swap, and its `before` is the state one tick before the end. The state before the burst lives only in `baseOps[0]`. Example: the draft derives as D0, and the user types `{a`, `{ac`, `{acc` into a pin field. That is one coalesced entry ending at D3, and none of those three drafts derives. On reload the page opens on D0. `stepsBackTo` compares D0 against D2, gets no match, and returns null, so the whole saved history is discarded. It should have found one step back. The same happens on the palette lab whenever the live state lags the history across a coalesced slider drag.
triage.cause: reads forwardOps where coalescing keeps the original before in baseOps

claim: Jump-to-token builds an unescaped attribute selector that throws on a token name containing `"` or `\`

triage.scenario: a definition pins a token whose key contains a double quote or backslash (pins are user-keyed); inspecting or jumping to it sets `highlight`, and `querySelector('[aria-label="a"b"]')` throws a SyntaxError inside the effect, taking the editor down. Should escape with `CSS.escape` (or compare `aria-label` values without a selector).

claim: A negative px value in a scale draws a full-width ladder bar

triage.scenario: Take a scale whose steps resolve to a negative length, such as a tracking or offset scale with `-1px`. `pxOf` accepts the minus sign and returns -1. The bar then gets `width: -N%`, which is invalid CSS, so the browser drops it. The bar is `display: block` with no width, so it spans the whole cell: the most negative step draws as the widest bar. `widest` also ignores magnitude, so a scale whose values are all negative gets `widest = 1`. The bar should scale by `Math.abs(px)` against the widest magnitude.
triage.cause: signed value used as a width

tokensReadAt follows custom-property declarations that a later or more specific rule overrides
Editing a pin in the token layers drops its `description` and `scope`
Click-to-inspect never reports tokens read through a custom property declared in an element's inline style

triage.scenario: In the theme editor, turn Inspect on and click the specimen Slider. `Slider` writes `thumbSize`/`trackHeight` as inline custom properties on its root (`style="--rp-thumb-size: var(--wzl-slider-thumb-size); --rp-track-height: var(--wzl-slider-track-h)"`, pinned by `Slider.metrics.test.tsx:24`). The stylesheet rules read `var(--rp-thumb-size)`, and `follow('rp-thumb-size', i)` looks for a declaration only among the `winners` built from `document.styleSheets`. It finds none, so `slider-thumb-size` and `slider-track-h` are never listed under "Tokens read", and a click cannot jump to them. An element's `style` attribute is a declaration in force, and it beats every stylesheet rule for that property. It should be folded into each chain element's winners (as the highest-ranked, non-important layer).
triage.cause: inline style declarations left out of the cascade

claim: tokensReadAt never visits rules from @import-ed stylesheets, so tokens declared there are missed

triage.scenario: a stylesheet that pulls in component CSS with `@import` has a `CSSImportRule` whose rules live on `rule.styleSheet.cssRules`, not `rule.cssRules`; `visit` recurses only through `cssRules`, so every token read by an imported sheet's declarations is missing from Inspect's list. Should visit `rule.styleSheet` (subject to its media) as well.

A reference field being edited closes mid-typing when the store normalizes the value that was set

triage.scenario: the field stays open only while `Object.is(editing.value, ctx.value)`. `onChange` records the raw typed value, then `ctx.setValue(value)`; a store whose validator coerces or trims (or rejects) the value hands back a different `ctx.value`, so `open` turns false, the text field is swapped for the reference chip, and focus is lost on the keystroke. Should hold open on the value the leaf reports after the write, or until blur.
